start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-jobs-handed-between-ais with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and ais [{\"id\": \"ai:codex-on-mac\", \"can\": [\"code\"], \"order\": 2, \"live\": {\"seen_at\": \"2026-11-18T03:00:00Z\", \"minutes\": 60}}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the AIs and jobs are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-jobs-handed-between-ais" with store and, when you have them, the AIs and jobs to keep.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example AIs and jobs: the prove step must give every expected answer, or the run stops and says which.

4. To hand a job or take one, your AI reads the AIs and jobs from the store, hands them to the authority tool as stored.records, and keeps each write the tool answers, conditioned on the value it read. The tool keeps nothing and reads no store.
5. Every later run keeps the new AIs and jobs and reads each one back; ask your AI who is live and how busy, and it reads the store's own objects.

worked_examples.title: Handing a job from one AI to another, kept in a person's own database
worked_examples.ask: Hand Codex the job of checking the deploy.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the AIs and jobs already kept in the tables ai and ai_job, made by an earlier run, and the prove step gave every expected answer.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept_ids ["ai:codex-on-mac"] and found_ids ["ai:codex-on-mac"]; the AI is in who-is-live for codex-on-mac.
